title: The agent that wouldn't stop
intro: Monday morning: a $340 API bill from an agent that ran all weekend. Open the clues and name the actual failure.

facts.label: The trace
facts.value: One run, thousands of steps: search → summarize → 'not quite right' → search again. The same three tool calls cycling for 61 hours.

facts.label: The loop condition
facts.value: The agent's instructions say 'continue until the report is comprehensive.' No attempt cap, no budget, no timeout anywhere in the run config.

facts.label: The evaluator
facts.value: There is none. The agent judges its own output inline — and its bar for 'comprehensive' drifts upward every cycle.

facts.label: The guardrails
facts.value: An input guardrail exists (blocks off-topic requests). Nothing watches the run itself — no output check, no cost check.

facts.label: The model
facts.value: Same model and temperature as every other successful run this month.

question: What actually failed?
choices: The model degraded over the weekend
Unbounded autonomy: no termination cap or budget, and no external evaluator to end the loop
The input guardrail was too strict
Search tools are inherently unsafe for agents
debrief: The trace shows a healthy agent doing exactly what it was told: 'continue until comprehensive' — a subjective bar, judged by itself, with no cap, no budget, no timeout, and no external evaluator to call time. The input guardrail is real but guards the wrong thing: it judges the request, not the run. The fix is the agentic loop's two most-skipped steps, made concrete: a termination condition (max attempts, token budget, wall-clock cap) and an EXTERNAL judge — an evaluator agent or graph node whose pass/fail ends the loop. Autonomy is granted per run, and every grant needs an expiry.
